{{MEinfobox
|name=Charge
|cg=Charge.png}}
{{StatusEffect|Charge|b}} is a Status Effect that is gained through various skills and is spent to improve skill effects. Charge Count decreases by 1 at the end of each turn. Most {{StatusEffect|Charge|b}} users only use Charge Count, while some also gain Charge Potency by spending Charge Count and use it for additional skill effects. Charge normally has a maximum Count of 20, although this can be increased through Passives or E.G.O Gifts (except for Identities with Potency-fixed Unique Charge; their maximum cannot be increased by external means).

{{StatusEffect|Charge|b}} is linked to the {{Icons|Envy}}Envy Sin Affinity.

==Strengths & Weaknesses==
{{StatusEffect|Charge|b}} is an easy Status Effect to use, as it only decreases from spending Charge or at Turn End. Charge-based Identities also usually deal high damage with high rolls on Skills that spend Charge Count, which makes them versatile. Another notable benefit of Charge is that {{StatusEffect|Charge|b}} Identities do not need a "Charge team" to function at full capacity. A high level Charge Identity can be placed on any team.

{{StatusEffect|Charge|b}} does not have particular strengths or weaknesses, with the exception that Charge Identities need a couple of turns to raise their SP and Charge Count in an Encounter before they can fight at full capacity. Several Charge Identities have significant punishments for using their Skill 3's without enough Charge, while others simply result in low rolls. Identities that rely on spending charge count to generate potency may instead have a Skill 3 that gains charge and have a Skill 2 that spends a large amount of charge. 

{{StatusEffect|Charge|b}} is the most effective against enemies weak to {{Icons|Envy}}Envy and {{Icons|Gloom}}Gloom due to the skill distributions of Charge Identities. Because they usually have extremely powerful Skill 3's, a Charge team can deal tremendous damage in a single turn if an opportunity arises (such as a Staggered enemy). 

{{StatusEffect|Charge|b}} Identities usually have powerful Uptie IV's that increase the rate at which they gain Charge, reducing the importance of having teammates or E.G.O to support Charge Count generation.

==Charge Potency==
While older {{StatusEffect|Charge|b}} Identities utilize only the Count, newer ones (almost all that have been released since [[Season 4: Clear All Cathy]]) can raise their Charge Potency by accumulating spent Charge Count throughout the Encounter. All Identities that can gain {{StatusEffect|Charge|b}} Potency gain it for every 10 cumulative {{StatusEffect|Charge|b}} Count spent throughout the encounter. Some Identities have this on a constantly active passive, while others only trigger it with a passive that needs [[Sin]] resources. In the latter case, only {{StatusEffect|Charge|b}} Count spent while the effect is active is counted.

{{StatusEffect|Charge|b}} Potency is not spent, and instead serves as a long-lasting benefit that requires a considerably longer time to accumulate than Charge Count.

All Identities start with 1 {{StatusEffect|Charge|b}} Potency, and Identities with 2+ Charge Potency will never lose Charge, even if the Count reaches 0 (except for Identities with Potency-fixed Unique Charge).

===Related Effects===

The debuffs {{StatusEffect|Photoelectricity|d}} and {{StatusEffect|Spark Discharge|d}} both allow attacking units to gain Charge upon hitting an enemy, with {{StatusEffect|Photoelectricity|d}} being the more stable of the two, being applied by an Identity and allowing attackers to gain up to 6 Charge Count per Skill.
